headline: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved variances for Costco and advanced a two-family housing bylaw, while committees prepared funding requests for town meeting.
synopsis: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved retaining wall and light pole height variances for Costco Wholesale at 21 Coslin Drive and voted to forward a draft two-family zoning bylaw to the Select Board for October Special Town Meeting. The Planning Board granted occupancy sign-off for Chase Bank at 154 Turnpike Road while continuing site plan reviews for 22 and 154 Turnpike Road. Both the Trails Committee and Golf Committee prepared supplemental Community Preservation Act requests ahead of fall town meeting to fund the Peninsula Trail footbridge and a course irrigation project. In addition, the Golf Committee reviewed resident complaints regarding errant balls damaging property on Latisquama Road, and the Tricentennial Committee advanced logistics for 2027 anniversary events.

highlights.title: Costco variances approved for retaining walls and lighting
highlights.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved variances allowing retaining walls up to 31 feet high and parking lot light poles up to 36.5 feet high at 21 Coslin Drive. Major site plan review for the project remains pending before the Planning Board.

highlights.title: Draft two-family zoning bylaw advanced to Select Board
highlights.why: The board unanimously approved a draft zoning amendment to submit to the Select Board for the October 17 Special Town Meeting warrant. The proposed bylaw formally defines two-family homes, removes an obsolete two-year conversion waiting period, and aligns local rules with state standards.

highlights.title: Trails Committee seeks additional CPA funds for footbridge
highlights.why: After construction bids exceeded initial budgets, the committee finalized an additional $226,096 CPA grant application to bring the total Stony Brook footbridge budget to $437,328 ahead of fall Special Town Meeting.

highlights.title: Golf Committee plans supplemental CPA request for irrigation
highlights.why: The committee submitted a supplemental CPA request for roughly $320,000 to $350,000 to complete financing for an estimated $970,000 course irrigation project slated for Town Meeting approval.

highlights.title: Northborough Road residential division hearing continued
highlights.why: A request for a special permit to divide an 8-acre parcel into two building lots served by a common driveway using an 1896 aqueduct right-of-way was continued to August 12 to consult Town Counsel regarding frontage legality.

highlights.title: Errant golf balls cause damage on Latisquama Road
highlights.why: Neighbors reported significant property damage and vehicle dents from errant balls near the 7th tee. The committee agreed to consult a golf course architect on potential hole redesigns or tee box adjustments.
